subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing & GPU SKU fit for CumulusAI deal
messages:
From: Alex Moretti <alex.moretti@cumulusai.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for inference - initial data

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this — we're finalizing architecture for the CumulusAI inference rollout and need Redwood's recommended dedicated fleet mix. High level requirements below: 

- Workloads: conversational assistant (token lengths up to ~2k), long-context retrieval generation, and a realtime embedding pipeline for similarity search.
- Peak traffic expectation: ~5k concurrent inference QPS (mix: 60% chat, 30% embeddings, 10% reranking).
- Latency SLO: 150 ms P95 for chat prompt-complete on average 1k tokens generated.
- Model candidates: we're evaluating a 70B dense model (production), and a smaller 7B quantized model for low-latency fanout.
- Data residency: US only.
- Budget: reserved committed spend, looking for predictable per-token inference cost while meeting SLOs.

Can you advise H100 vs A100 vs L4 tradeoffs for a Dedicated cluster (memory footprint, throughput, real-world latency, and operational fallbacks)? Also need an initial sizing estimate (node counts) and a short ops fallback strategy (e.g., burst to hosted or failover to smaller quantized model).

Attachments: I'll share an internal MAP spreadsheet right after.

Appreciate any quick guidance — we are on a tight procurement timeline (sign by mid-June).

Best,
Alex
Director of Platform Engineering
Cumulus AI

Quick summary of what we'll deliver in the next 24-48h:
- A recommended primary SKU mix for Dedicated (H100/A100/L4) sized to your peak and SLOs.
- Memory and throughput tradeoffs per SKU with realistic per-node concurrency targets.
- Estimated node counts for a committed pool and recommended burst capacity (both dedicated and hosted fallback).
- A concise ops fallback playbook (quantized model fallback, regional routing, and graceful degradation).

Marcus — see Alex's workload notes above and the MAP link: https://drive.redwood.com/s/Cumulus-MAP-v1. Key constraints: 150 ms P95 on ~1k generation tokens, 5k peak QPS mix, US-only. Please focus on: effective batch sizing for chat, KV cache strategies for long context, and how much GPU memory is needed for 70B vs 7B.

Lauren — once Marcus provides counts/cost delta, can you include a redline of expected monthly committed spend and suggested commit band that maps to their budget ask?

Alex — expect a follow-up with a short recommendation and an attached CSV with per-node throughput numbers.

Thanks,

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for inference - initial data

Karthik / Lauren — dug into the MAP and ran quick perf estimates. Below are our recommendations and assumptions. I attached sku_fitment_estimates.csv with measured per-node p95s from recent benchmarks; I'll paste the highlights here.

Assumptions (workload):
- Production model: 70B dense (fp16) ~ requires ~80 GB GPU memory for KV cache + activations at 2k context if unsharded; with sharded KV/cache we can target ~48-56 GB effective per-GPU for inference depending on runtime config.
- Latency target: 150 ms P95 for generation of ~1k tokens (note: longer generation amplifies tail variance; recommend server-side prefix caching where possible).
- Concurrency mix: chat-heavy; batching opportunity ~ up to 8 concurrent small requests per GPU for chat (1-2 token prefixes) and larger per-request batch for generative workloads.

SKU tradeoffs (practical):
- H100 (80GB): Pros: best single-card throughput for large-context 70B, lower model sharding complexity, headroom for concurrent KV caches, better fp8/fp16 perf on newer kernels. Cons: higher cost per-hour, less available capacity in some clouds.
- A100 (80GB/40GB options): Pros: mature drivers, wide availability; A100-80GB close to H100 for memory but lower throughput on some attention kernels. A100-40 good fit for 7B quantized model and embedding pipelines. Cons: for 70B you'll need more sharding across cards and interconnect bandwidth matters.
- L4 (48GB, quantized TF32/INT8): Pros: excellent cost-efficiency for 7B-size and quantized 70B variants if acceptable; very good for embedding at high QPS. Cons: memory limit for 70B dense — would require model quantization + kernel supports; latency for long-generation can degrade.

Concrete recommendation (primary fleet + hedges):
1) Primary committed pool: mix of H100 and A100-80GB
   - H100 nodes (for 70B dense production): aim for 12 H100 GPUs (3 nodes x 4x-GPU if using 4x per server) — expected effective concurrent sessions: ~800-1,000 chat qps at target latency assuming optimized batching and prefix caching.
   - A100-80GB nodes (for additional concurrency and redundancy): 16 A100 GPUs (4 nodes x 4x-GPU) — serves mid-size requests, embeddings, and helps shard heavy models to increase throughput.
   - Rationale: H100 handles the bulk of the long-context generation workload where low tail latency is critical. A100 provides extra capacity and cost balance.

2) Quantized L4 fleet for scale and embeddings (burst/baseline):
   - 32 L4 GPUs (8 nodes x 4x-GPU) as burstable capacity behind a routing policy: embeddings-heavy and lightweight 7B traffic go to L4. For degraded conditions or cost-saving mode, route non-critical traffic to L4-quantized models.

3) Fallbacks & operational playbook:
- Primary fallback: automatic routing to A100 pool if H100 capacity saturated (transparent to the client, slightly higher latency for some queries).
- Secondary fallback: for non-critical flows, route to L4-quantized variant (20-30% quality delta expected for some prompts; validate with warm eval set).
- Emergency: overflow to Redwood hosted API (short-term burst) via signed tokens; reserve a small hosted pool to cover 10% peak QPS as last-line option.

Estimated steady committed sizing to meet 5k peak with SLO: 
- Committed H100 GPUs: 12
- Committed A100 GPUs: 16
- Reserved L4 (burstable): 32 (can be on-demand or committed at a lower band)

Cost delta & notes for Lauren: expect H100 committed unit costs ~2x A100 for equivalent provisioned hours — we should model several commit bands (small/medium/large) to find the sweet spot for their budget. Also call out that inter-node networking (NVLink/PCIe) and scheduler placement affects p95; if they require single-rack latency guarantees, that increases cost.

Attachments: sku_fitment_estimates.csv (per-node p95s, tokens/sec, memory usage) and ops-fallback-playbook.pdf (short checklist for failover).

Let me know if you want me to convert the estimate into a node-count per-rack layout and a short TCO.

- Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Moretti <alex.moretti@cumulusai.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for inference - initial data

Alex — attaching the two files Marcus referenced and summarizing our recommendation for your procurement team: 

Summary recommendation (short):
- Commit band: start with a mid-band commit of 12 H100 GPUs + 16 A100-80GB GPUs, with an L4 burst pool (recommended on-demand to start, convert to committed later).
- Why: H100 provides headroom and best p95 for 70B long-context generation; A100 expands concurrency and lowers marginal cost; L4 is the cost-efficient path for embeddings and quantized 7B.
- Ops playbook: primary route to H100/A100; overflow to A100; degraded quality mode routes non-critical traffic to L4 quantized models; emergency overflow to Redwood hosted API (we can maintain a reserved burst credit to avoid cold starts).

Next steps and asks for Cumulus procurement:
1) Confirm target commit start date and preferred cloud/provider (we recommend region-specific capacity placement — single-region US-east preferred).
2) Share any hard budget ceiling per month so Lauren can map to commit bands and provide a pricing proposal.
3) Approve a short eval run (1 week) where we route ~10% of live traffic to the L4 quantized path to validate regression on your key prompts.

Attachments: Cumulus-MAP-v1.xlsx; sku_fitment_estimates.csv; ops-fallback-playbook.pdf

If that looks good, I'll loop in our procurement lead to start contract sketches and can provide sample commit tiers and estimated monthly cost next business day.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
